statement: Sam starts at 30 and counts backwards in steps of 5. He does not say 30. What is the fourth number he says?

choices.misconception: I gave the first number I said rather than the fourth.
I stopped after only two steps.
I counted 30 as the first number I said, but the count starts after 30.
I counted one step too far and said five numbers.

hints: Say the numbers out loud and keep track with your fingers.
Count down in fives and raise a finger for each number you say, starting after 30. Stop when four fingers are up, rather than when the numbers run out.

solutions.reliable: Counting down from 30 gives 25, 20, 15, 10, so the fourth number is 10. The idea to keep: the starting number is not one of the steps, so count the steps rather than the numbers you can see.

whyOnTest: Whether the starting number counts as a step is the whole difficulty, and the three nearby answers are all off by one step.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
